articleHeadline: Trivalent Antiviral Conjugates Trap Influenza Viruses by Cross-Linking Them
articleSummary: Influenza antiviral strategy expanded with multivalent antiviral conjugates (AVCs) tethered to an Fc fragment, developed by researchers from the Academy of Military Medical Sciences in Beijing with Tsinghua University, Xiamen University and the University of Hong Kong. Using click chemistry, the team built mono-, di-, and tri-valent zanamivir-Fc (AVC-Z1–Z3) and a tri-valent peramivir-Fc (AVC-P3). Tri-valent AVC-Z3 showed superior antiviral activity and, crucially, induced inter-virion aggregation by cross-linking neuraminidase-bearing virions, producing a dual-stage inhibition that blocks both entry and release. AVC-P3 displayed stronger in vitro activity and a longer in vivo half-life than AVC-Z3 and CD388 with YTE. In mouse models challenged with H1N1, H3N2, H5N1, and influenza B, AVC-P3 outperformed other AVCs, baloxavir, and CD388, suggesting broad, long-acting prophylactic/therapeutic potential against diverse influenza A and B threats.

articleSummary: Globally, about 2.3 million cancer cases in 2024 were attributable to infections, representing roughly 12% of all new cancers. articleHeadline: The genetic technique that made it possible to identify COVID-19 and detect almost any infection
articleSummary: Metagenomic analysis sequences DNA and RNA from patient samples to identify all organisms present, distinguishing bacteria from viruses, enabling rapid, precisely targeted treatments. Notably, a UCSF team led by Charles Chiu developed a metagenomic test for cerebrospinal fluid that uncovered hepatitis E as the cause of meningitis and liver failure in a woman awaiting liver transplant, preventing surgery and guiding antiviral therapy. In London, two hospitals found pathogens not detected by standard tests in about 30% of respiratory infections. This capability could help alert authorities to emerging outbreaks.

articleSummary: Giardia duodenalis circulates widely across Brazil’s human, animal, and environmental compartments, but surveillance is fragmented. A decade of Brazilian studies (114 published 2016–March 2026) was analyzed; only nine (7.9%) evaluated two or more compartments simultaneously. In animals, dogs 0.75–50%, cats 2.02–24.8%, cattle/buffalo 2.0–26.75%, wildlife 2.94–59%, and captive non-human primates 83.3% vs 20% in the wild. The review highlights fragmented One Health surveillance of giardiasis in Brazil.

articleHeadline: Kissing bugs spread across the Americas in three great waves tied to
articleSummary: Kissing bugs (Triatominae), vectors of the parasite causing Chagas disease, spread across the Americas in three major waves over ~60 million years, with dispersal tied to global paleotemperatures. The most recent common ancestor is dated at ~59.2 million years ago, with likely origins in northern South America and parts of Mesoamerica, though Central or northern South America remains plausible. A time calibrated phylogeny using >2,500 ultraconserved elements and Dominican amber fossils analyzed 96 species across 11 bioregions. Dispersal-extinction-cladogenesis modelling and 6,591 stochastic mappings reveal three phases: Phase A (60–50 Ma) high dispersal from Amazonia to northern South America and into Mesoamerica, and Caatinga to Cerrado; Phase B (50–30 Ma) declines, with movements among Mesoamerica and northern South America toward Páramos, Caatinga, and Chaco; Phase C (30 Ma–present) resurgence with complex bidirectional dispersals, aided by the Isthmus of Panama and routes from Amazonia to Páramos and Caatinga, along with Caatinga–Atlantic Forest exchanges. Climate shifts (warm Paleocene–Eocene, cooler Oligocene, Miocene–Pleistocene fluctuations) coincide with the pattern, illuminating the historical reach of Chagas disease vectors.

articleHeadline: Ghana's Nurses Face Hepatitis B Risk as Vaccination Follow-Through
articleSummary: Hepatitis B risk among healthcare workers in Kumasi, Ghana, was highlighted in a cross-sectional study of 625 staff across four hospitals (Nov–Dec 2023), published in BMC Health Services Research. While 61.6% had completed the recommended three-dose Hepatitis B vaccine, only 15.2% of the fully vaccinated had undergone post‑vaccination antibody testing, and just 25.4% were aware such testing existed. Needlestick injuries occurred in 34.9% of participants. Clinicians faced nearly ninefold higher odds of injury than other roles; permanent staff about twice as likely to be injured. Vaccination completion was higher among older workers (31–40 years, >3x vs younger), married individuals (>2x), and occupational groups—laboratory scientists ~4x, nurses/midwives ~3x—compared with others. Permanent staff were more likely to know about, and actually undergo, antibody testing, suggesting workforce design influences preventive care. Limitations include purposive sampling and cross‑sectional design, potentially limiting generalizability to the Ashanti Region.
